Causes of Cancer
Mutation may cause over stimulation of oncogene to produce proteins, or gene or chromosome duplication can result in more copies of the gene
rasgene family most commonly affected
BRCA1 in breast cancer
Mutations or chromosome deletions can result in abnormal or missing tumor suppressors
of all human cancers have broken or missing p53 gene
Many more examples you may find in future courses
explanation: Mutations can lead to cancer by overstimulating proto-oncogenes to form oncogenes, or through gene/chromosome duplications that increase gene copy number. The ras gene family is the most commonly affected proto-oncogene family, and BRCA1 is a well-known example linked to breast cancer. Conversely, mutations or chromosome deletions can result in abnormal or missing tumor suppressors. Notably, approximately half (1/2) of all human cancers are associated with a broken or missing p53 tumor suppressor gene.

questions.q: Approximately what fraction of all human cancers are associated with a broken or missing p53 tumor suppressor gene?
questions.exp: The slide states that half (1/2) of all human cancers have a broken or missing p53 gene.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an oncogene/gene family mentioned on this page?
questions.exp: The slide lists the ras gene family (and BRCA1 in breast cancer) as examples where mutations can cause overstimulation.
